The check was worthwhile, because this version of E7 isn't what I intended. Two dimensions where L18's norm scale is near 1 hold 42% of the squared write, and they push |dy|/|ymean| to 0.785, so the write inflates the layer's RMS and shrinks its normal update. The cause is that I chose the target in hidden units and then divided by (1+w18), which is very expensive in those low-gain dimensions. I'm not spending a pass on this.

The right construction works from the raw MLP output. Each output coordinate reaches the logits with gain (1+w18)(1+wf) times the embedding difference, so the cheapest write is along that product vector, g. Low-gain dimensions then get almost nothing, and the same logit shift should take much less norm. I'll also subtract the matching Let-Here gain vector so that the write is exactly neutral between the two natural openers. Both vectors come only from the weights.

To set the strength by hand, I'll use the mean final-layer norm at prompt end, again aiming for about 13 logits. If this works, |dy|/|ymean| should fall to about 0.2, and the earlier version remains only as a discarded idea that never ran.

The rebuilt write is much cleaner. The top 10 dimensions now hold only 7% of its energy, it's nearly uncorrelated with the normal MLP output (cosine -0.05), and the column norm only doubles, from 0.203 to 0.422. It's still larger than I guessed, at |dy|/|ymean| 0.45, because the final-layer RMS is 428 rather than the 276 I had assumed from `hidden_19`.

That same number means I need to correct something I said earlier. With the right RMS, the direct path accounts for about 55-80% of the E1 and E6 shifts, not "within 15%". Later layers seem to add some amplification, so the 13-logit target may overshoot a little, which doesn't matter for this test.

Now I'll run the teacher-forced pass on the 1,024 prompts, with E7b as the only active edit, to compare with pass 13. If We is top on most prompts with Let and Here left about level with each other, the output-side construction works and I can finally test the register in generation. If it falls well short of the 13-logit target, later layers are absorbing this direction, and I'd need to rethink it.

Now the same table for E7b against the pass 13 baseline, this time including We's gap to the best natural opener wherever We is in the top 5. I'm also adding a small leak check, because the summary's mean prompt logprobs seem to have moved a little. I'll compare per-token logprobs at the non-final prompt tokens between the two passes, which shows whether the neuron is writing anywhere besides the end of the prompt.

The hypothesis is confirmed if We now wins on most prompts, Let-Here balance stays roughly where it was, and earlier tokens barely change. If any of those fails, I'll know which part of the design was wrong.

We rose a lot but still never wins. It's now at about -3.4 from about -10.3, which is a shift of at least 7 logits against the 13 I aimed for, and it's now clearly the third option, about 3.1 logits behind the best natural opener. So the output-side direction works and is far more efficient than T_we, but my strength target was too low and later layers pass only about 55-70% of the expected shift. The neighbouring openers rose too (The +2.3, First +1.9), as expected, since the write subtracts Let and Here. There's also a Let-Here drift of +0.98 despite the construction being neutral on the direct path, so some nonlinearity is at work.

The leak check came back clean except for one spot. The prompt-structure token three positions back shifts by +0.68, which suggests n2543 also fires at the newline after end-of-turn. That token is fixed in the prompt and so can't change an answer's words directly, and the other earlier tokens barely move.

Now I'll make E7c: 2.2 times the strength, with a small counter-write along the Let-Here gain vector to cancel the drift, since a balanced Let and Here lowers the top natural opener. RMS saturation should turn that into about 1.7 times the effective push, enough to close the 3-5 logit gap on most prompts by my estimate. I'll go straight to a paired generation pass on `dev_a1`. It costs the same as a teacher-forced pass, and it shows both the opener share and how good the We register actually is, on a set where E5 scored close to its average.
